The issue in the code is that the end of the range is being calculated incorrectly. Specifically, the line `range.add(L + (1L << i) - 1);` is causing the end of the range to be one less than it should be. This is because the sequence should include `L + (1L << i)`, not `L + (1L << i) - 1`.

To fix this, we need to adjust the end of the range calculation to correctly include the last element of the sequence.

Here is the patch:

# modification 1
```
<file>faultyVersion.java</file>
<original>
            range.add(L + (1L << i) - 1);
</original>
<patched>
            range.add(L + (1L << i));
</patched>
```

This change ensures that the end of the range is correctly calculated, and the sequence includes the last element as required by the problem statement.
